extracted.intended_audience: senior strategic communication leaders (chief communication officers, CCOs)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and expectations for senior strategic communication leaders (CCOs) and their teams regarding professional conduct, community membership, learning, and the role of communications in advancing organizational trust, reputation, and societal benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace the highest professional standards
rubrics_metrics.description: We advance this mission by embracing the highest professional standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a core organizational value: members and leaders should uphold exemplary professional conduct in communication practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership criteria — exclusive assembly of top practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Page’s membership criteria ensure it remains an exclusive assembly of the very best and brightest of the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership is selective to maintain a high-caliber peer group; implies standards for experience, seniority, and demonstrated leadership in communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desire to learn and live by the Page Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Our members share in common a desire to learn from one another’s experiences and challenges and live by the Page Principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members are expected to engage in peer learning and to adhere to the Page Principles as behavioral/ethical norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a collegial and dynamic learning environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Providing a collegial and dynamic learning environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page advances its mission by creating environments (programs, peer networking, learning offerings) that support ongoing professional development and team development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance how communications is understood, practiced, and taught
rubrics_metrics.description: Advancing the way that communications is understood, practiced and taught.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should work to evolve the profession through thought leadership, improved practice, and education initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilitate connection, insight-sharing, and practical tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Page helps members to connect and share insights on the many challenges facing their organizations, fresh thinking and useful tools, plus several programs to help develop their teams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization values practical exchange — sharing challenges, new ideas, and actionable tools — and running programs aimed at team capability building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operate honestly, responsibly and respectfully toward all stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: The CCO has the opportunity and responsibility to ensure that organizations operate honestly, responsibly and respectfully toward all stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical conduct toward stakeholders is a core expectation for communication leaders and informs decision-making and public messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and activate corporate character
rubrics_metrics.description: By defining and activating corporate character, the CCO helps the enterprise earn public trust, protect reputation and preserve its license to operate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CCOs should articulate and operationalize an organization's values and character so they are reflected in actions and communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Earn public trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Help the enterprise earn public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public trust is presented as an explicit outcome CCOs should aim for through authentic, consistent communication and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect reputation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputation protection is a stated objective tied to corporate character and communications strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve the license to operate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintaining social and stakeholder legitimacy for the organization is an explicit responsibility of communications leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance financial success with societal benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong CCO leadership ensures companies not only succeed financially, but contribute to the benefit of society, as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications leadership should align business objectives with broader societal contributions, signaling a dual accountability to shareholders and society.
